newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: KOF sees modest Swiss rate increases in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: KOF sees modest Swiss rate increases in 1997/98.

text.p: The Swiss KOF economic research institute, part of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, said it expected only a moderate rise in Swiss interest rates through to end 1998, against the background of some likely improvement in the economy.
KOF is forecasting Swiss gross domestic product (GDP) growth in 1997 of 0.3 percent and growth of 1.6 percent in 1998. GDP fell 0.7 percent in 1996.

In its spring forecast KOF said: "The SNB will at first stick to its current tack in the 1997/98 forecast period. There appears to be no danger of inflation despite a substantial growth of the money supply."

It forecast central bank money supply, versus the fourth quarter of the previous year, to expand by 1.0 percent in 1997 and by 0.2 percent in 1998. This compared with a robust 5.0 percent expansion in 1996.
KOF expected the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to continue with its relatively expansive monetary policy until the economy begins to show definite signs of improvement.

"Monetary policy is expected to tighten only once there are clearer signs that the business cycle is emerging from its current spell of weakness. This is likely to be the case in the second half of this year," KOF said.
KOF cited inflation-dampening factors such as competition brought about by the new regulations in the domestic market, and anti-trust laws.

These "will combine with continued under-utilisation of production capacity to counteract the inflationary effect of the higher import prices resulting from the (Swiss) franc's downward slide," KOF said.
It forecast an inflation rate of 1.0 percent for 1997 and 1.2 percent for 1998, compared with 0.8 percent in 1996.
KOF said the franc could again firm somewhat as a result of European economic and monetary union (EMU) and likely narrowing of the interest rate differential vis-a-vis Germany.
Any franc strength should also weigh against excessive monetary tightening.

"Since the economic situation will remain shaky for the time being, and because the franc is likely to come under renewed upward pressure as the third stage of EMU approaches (1998), there will be be only cautious moves to increase the restrictiveness of monetary policy," KOF said.

"Thus interest rates are anticipated to rise only moderately by the end of 1998," it said. It added that by then, three-month Euro Swiss franc rates could have risen to 2.6 percent and the federal bond yield to 4.1 percent.
Three-month Eurofrancs were quoted around 1-3/4 percent on Tuesday. The 10-year federal bond yield was at 3.75 percent.

With respect to the Swiss franc, KOF said: "After depreciating by an average of 8.6 percent in the current year, the franc can expect an upward revaluation of 2.8 percent in real terms in 1998," KOF said.
The Swiss franc traded at 85.85 centimes to the mark early Tuesday, and at 1.4715 francs to the dollar.
